The other day I went out to lunch with my mom and we were talking about my son. In response to something my son said, she asked me if they still tell kids "sticks and stones my break my bones, but words will never hurt me." I don't think I ever explicitly said that to my son on account of I don't tend to parent in slogans, plus I do my best to encourage him to be as badass as possible in all situations.

I ended up telling her that no people tend to teach their kids the opposite nowadays and filled her in on trigger warnings and safe spaces and she was fairly horrified. But it still made me wonder about that phrase. Does modern society consider it to be wrong and an outdated relic? Like I remember when I heard it as a kid, it was kind of a call to action to find your inner strength and rise above your own insecurities. Now anymore it seems like people want to wallow in them and it is completely inexplicable to me.

But yeah, even though in my head it sounds like a cliche, that whole sticks and stones thing might have more merit than I originally gave it credit for just because it calls on kids to demand more of themselves and their own resilience in the face of perceived adversity. I haven't heard it uttered in a while and it'd be nice if it made a comeback among parents or anyone kids pay attention to.
